title: Throughput Safety Net and Rollback Clauses for Dedicated Capacity SLAs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a readable, enforceable SLA and associated operational procedures for Dedicated capacity customers that combines quantile-driven throughput guarantees, an explicit error-budget model, automated credit calculation, and a contractual rollback/mitigation clause triggered by sustained degradation. This ticket synthesizes product, ops, and legal requirements into a single deliverable for sales attachments.
background: Customers on Dedicated capacity need predictable serve rates and commercial remedies when we miss. Existing artifacts focus on credit formulas or static thresholds; this initiative introduces an integrated ‘safety net’ approach: tiered error budget bands, short- and long-window measurements, autoscaler interlocks that protect committed capacity, and a contractual rollback path for severe degradations. The goal is to balance legal clarity with operational practicality.
goal: Ship SLA definitions and contract language covering: (1) measurable throughput SLOs (quantile + sliding window), (2) error budget math and credit computation, (3) autoscaler/fleet interlock rules, (4) escalation and rollback clauses, and (5) monitoring & reporting requirements. Deliverables: legal appendix text, engineering acceptance criteria, and runbook links.
acceptance_criteria: SLA document with precise metric definitions (units, aggregation, windows) approved by legal and sales
Error budget formula documented with examples and credit schedule (automated calculator spec)
Autoscale interlock spec that defines how Dedicated autoscaler behaves when SLOs are at risk
Fleet control requirements (priority routing, burst pools, failover ordering) enumerated for engineering implementation
Rollout and rollback contractual clause drafted and reviewed by legal that includes notice windows and remediation timelines
Observability requirements (dashboards + alerts) and daily report template for customers finalized
Integration tests and smoke checks defined to validate measurement pipeline for SLOs
sla_definitions: Primary SLA metric = ServeRate95: the 95th percentile of tokens-served-per-minute per-customer over a 24-hour sliding window, measured every 5 minutes. Secondary metric = P99-latency-windowed: 99th percentile tail latency for response generation for requests classified as 'committed' during the same 24-hour window. A customer is considered degraded if ServeRate95 falls below their committed tokens/minute entitlement for >= 15 consecutive minutes OR if ServeRate95 underperforms the committed rate for >= 1 hour in the 24-hour window. Aggregation rules, timezone conventions, and how partial-minute samples are handled are specified in the annex.
error_budget_formula: ErrorBudgetPercentage = max(0, 100 * (CommittedRate - ObservedServeRate95) / CommittedRate). ErrorBudgetWindow = rolling 24 hours. RemainingErrorBudget = sum of positive minute-level deficits; when RemainingErrorBudget > 0 the customer is in breach of the error budget. Credits are computed proportional to the time-weighted deficit and the committed monthly invoice for the Dedicated reservation.
credit_calculation_examples: Example A: Customer committed 1,200,000 tokens/min. Observed ServeRate95 averaged 1,080,000 tokens/min for a contiguous 2-hour window. Deficit = 120,000 tokens/min (10%). Time-weighted deficit = 10% * 2/720 (two hours out of 30 days) => credit = 0.0278% of monthly committed fee.

Example B: Short spike: 15 minutes at 50% of committed rate triggers automatic monitoring but is excluded from long-window remediation if 24-hour rolling ServeRate95 remains >= committed. Short-form credits apply only if deficit persists beyond the 1-hour threshold.
autoscale_interlock_rules: When RemainingErrorBudget > 0 (breach), autoscaler must prioritize remediation of committed capacity by: (1) suspending non-committed burst scaling that would divert GPU capacity away from committed pools, (2) temporarily increasing min replicas for committed pools up to configured safety cap, (3) triggering fast-path kernel selection and reduced batching strategies to favor latency and throughput rather than cost efficiency. Autoscaler must record each interlock event with a justification tag and link to the incident. Interlock cooldown: 30 minutes after error budget restoration before normal autoscale policies resume.
fleet_control_requirements: Fleet controls must expose: priority routing tags (committed, best-effort), weighted failover order (same-AZ first, then cross-AZ), burst pool sizing per customer, and a manual 'guarantee-lock' that ops can flip to give a customer temporary absolute priority for remediation. Controls must include a quota accounting view and an API for programmatic overrides with audit logging. Implementation must not require customer-side changes.
monitoring_and_alerting: Customer-facing dashboard tile showing ServeRate95 vs committed entitlement, RemainingErrorBudget, and recent interlock events
Ops alert: trigger P1 channel if RemainingErrorBudget > 0 for any customer for more than 30 minutes
Automated daily digest to customer (for those with active commitments) summarizing 24h SLOs, any credits earned, and mitigation steps taken
Synthetic checks per region every 1 minute that exercise committed-weight request shapes to validate end-to-end path
contract_snippets: Service Commitment: Redwood will provide dedicated serving capacity such that, over any rolling 24-hour period, the 95th percentile of tokens served per minute meets or exceeds the Customer's Committed Rate, subject to the Measurement & Exclusions section.

Error Budget & Credits: If observed performance falls below the Committed Rate per the agreed measurement for longer than the remediation thresholds, Customer will be eligible for credits computed per the Credit Schedule. Credits are customer remedies and not a substitute for equitable operational remediation.

Emergency Rollback: If sustained degradation exceeds the Severe Degradation threshold (defined as RemainingErrorBudget > 20% for > 6 hours), Customer may request an emergency rollback to an alternate prioritized fleet or accept a rescoped temporary entitlement. Redwood will respond within the Notification Window and document actions taken.
Exclusions: Outages caused by customer-side networking, force majeure, or customer-configured overrides are excluded from credit computation. Scheduled maintenance with >72 hours notice is excluded.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Draft SLA + legal review (this ticket)
Week 2: Engineering spec for measurement pipeline and autoscaler interlocks; define APIs for fleet controls
Week 3: Implement measurement plumbing and dashboard mock; create automated credit calculator (internal)
Week 4: Run closed pilot with 2 strategic customers and ops runbook validation
Week 5: Incorporate feedback, finalize contract appendix and go/no-go for GA
Week 6: GA release and sales enablement pack (templates + FAQ)
notes: We intend to keep the credit model simple (proportional % of committed invoice) to reduce billing complexity.
Legal emphasized explicit notice windows and a right for Redwood to propose temporary mitigations before credits are applied.
Engineering wants to avoid per-minute customer billing variance; suggest using daily aggregates for invoicing while keeping minute-level detection for ops action.
open_questions: Should Severe Degradation threshold be absolute (RemainingErrorBudget > 20%) or relative to historical variability for the customer?
What is the maximum allowable temporary entitlement reduction (if any) during emergency rollback to keep safety and avoid data loss for customer workloads?
How granular should credits be invoiced (daily bucket vs monthly statement)?
